• Global atmospheric concentrations of carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide have all risen significantly over recent decades. EPA’s Atmospheric Concentrations of Greenhouse Gases indicator provides an extended time series with ice code measurements that show that the current global atmospheric concentrations of carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide are unprecedented compared with the past 800,000 years.
  • All four future scenarios show projected greenhouse gas concentrations continuing to increase in the near term. However, the scenarios diverge widely over the rest of this century as a result of different assumptions about global economic development patterns and the extent to which the world reduces greenhouse gas emissions. The lowest emissions scenario shows carbon dioxide concentrations decreasing by the second half of this century, and several scenarios show decreases in methane.
  • Differences between scenarios for carbon dioxide follow the expected order from highest to lowest emission scenario. The other two gases show patterns that do not correlate directly with scenario order, as they reflect different assumptions about economic development, fuel switching, and more.
